newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria deploys troops in troubled oil town.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria deploys troops in troubled oil town.

text.p: Nigeria's military authorities said on Wednesday that soldiers had been sent into the troubled oil-producing town of Warri in the midwest to restore order.
"The troops were sent in yesterday to complement the efforts of the police and their job is to help restore normalcy," defence headquarters spokesman Colonel Godwin Ugbo told Reuters.

Anarchy has reigned in Warri, 300 kms (190 miles) west of Lagos since March 22 when clashes between armed youths broke out over the transfer of the local council headquarters from an Ijaw town to that of the rival Itsekiri tribe.
The death toll has risen to about 65 since April 12 when clashes resumed. A curfew imposed after the March clashes was lifted last week.

The independent Guardian newspaper reported on Wednesday that latest victims included a policeman while the Punch, also independent, said a policeman had been kidnapped by rioters and several women abducted.
State radio reported that the police had begun mass arrests of suspected rioters following the abductions.
"The presence of the military will restore confidence in civilians that they are being protected and forestall a complete breakdown of law and order," Ugbo said.

Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit, which pumps roughly half Nigeria's oil output of about two million barrels per day (bpd), said it had closed one flow station and output was running 2,000 bpd below normal.

At the height of the crisis in March, armed Ijaw tribesmen occupied six Shell oil flow stations, shutting off 100,000 bpd. A total of 127 of Shell's Nigerian staff held hostage by the tribesmen were released after negotiations and oil output has since resumed.
A navy ship was sent to Warri last weekend to ensure that oil production, Nigeria's economic backbone, was not affected.
